name: Sourced claim: source leads
when: The voice names the source before the claim ("According to the New York Times, ..."). The source box opens big and alone over the blurred shot, then steps aside to the lower third while the shot turns sharp, and the claim builds under it. Its ground changes (`ground`): the shot starts blurred and dimmed and turns sharp from `dock` over 22 frames (0.73 s).
anchor: The scene starts as the voice names the source (the box opens 0.13 s in); `dock` is where the voice moves on to the claim; each word (`at1`...`at9`) lands as the voice says it.

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.source: the words before the outlet: Reported by, According to, Confirmed by
vars.outlet: the outlet's name. Shown as text when there is no logo, else the logo's alt text
vars.logo: the outlet's logo file: build_video.mjs fills it from the repo's assets/logos/ when the outlet is listed in logos.json (or give a file the user supplied); empty = the sentence ends on the outlet's name as text
vars.logo_h: the logo's height in px: about 38 for a wordmark (Edge 37.7, The New York Times 36.8), 30 for a very long one (Game Informer), 44 for IGN, 61 for a square mark (Rockstar)
vars.logo_trim: px taken off the box's right padding after the logo: 14 for a square mark such as Rockstar's, else 0
vars.dock: seconds after the start: when the box shrinks to the lower third (the blurred ground starts to fade out at the same time)
vars.line1: the claim's first line, as the voice says it
vars.line2: the claim's second line; empty = a one-line claim
vars.at1: seconds after the start: when the claim's first word lands (its start in the voice)
vars.at2: the same for word 2. Words count across both lines. 0 = 4 frames after the previous word
vars.at3: the same for word 3 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word)
vars.at4: the same for word 4 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word)
vars.at5: the same for word 5 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word)
vars.at6: the same for word 6 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word)
vars.at7: the same for word 7 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word)
vars.at8: the same for word 8 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word)
vars.at9: the same for word 9 (0 = 4 frames after the previous word). A tenth word or more has no value: each lands 4 frames after the previous one
vars.out: seconds after the start: when it starts to leave (the scene ends 0.23 s later)

changed: The box steps aside in 15 frames instead of 18, so it lands in 0.5 s. The soft bottom-left dim baked into the lab's sharp footage is a layer of the template: it comes in over the 22 frames the shot takes to turn sharp and leaves with the exit. The blurred copy of the shot and its crossfade are the `ground` (the validated clip's exact filter, sharp from `dock` over its 22 frames), baked by the project; the validated crossfade eased sine.inOut, which the ground's crossfade has no field for. The source, the claim's lines and each word's time are values; the logo is a file from the project (empty = the outlet's name as text), with logo_h and logo_trim in place of the lab's per-outlet sizes.
